clue.text: Fats, I fancy, keeps closer to Billie Holiday

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the shuffled letters wrap around the next piece
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, signalling the letters are rearranged
the closer to a word is its final letter, here the end of Billie

explanation.surface: A jazz fan imagines a heavyweight figure keeping close company with the singer Billie Holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billie Holiday' reads as one name, but Holiday is the definition. 'fancy' shuffles FATS and I into FISTA, which 'keeps' the E closing Billie.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive holiday or celebration, originally in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Best bargain for Apple users?

parts.note: Apple names its products with a leading lower-case i (iPhone, iPad), so their version of anything starts with I
a bargain is a good deal

explanation.surface: A question about the best offer going for owners of Apple gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'i-deal' would be the Apple-branded bargain, in the style of iPhone and iPod.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, the best possible.

clue.text: Stumped by point about reduced internet connection speed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pieces go round the shortened connection

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: wifi is a wireless internet connection
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a sharp remark about their slow broadband speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' sounds like bafflement but is cricket's scorecard ST; 'point' is a headland, as in place names ending -ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness is the quality of being fast, which is a synonym for speed.

clue.text: A cross to head off trouble

definitions.text: A cross to head off trouble

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here the start of trouble

explanation.surface: A crucifix worn as a charm to ward off misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and also the recipe: A, a cross-bred animal, then the first letter of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to protect against evil or bad luck, and a cross can serve as one.

clue.text: University student finally acquiring a cracking degree?

definitions.text: University student finally acquiring a cracking degree?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking open, so the small pieces go inside the word for degree

parts.note: a grade is a degree or level on a scale

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of student

explanation.surface: A student at last earning an excellent degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like praise for the degree but tells U, A and T to break into GRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate is someone who has completed a university course and been awarded a degree.

clue.text: Me, I have a waggy tongue extremely disposed to do this?

definitions.text: Me, I have a waggy tongue extremely disposed to do this?

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out, so these letters are put in a new order
extremely means taking only the extreme ends, the first and last letters of tongue

explanation.surface: A self-confessed gossip admits being inclined to let slip a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' seems to mean inclined, but signals the anagram of ME I HAVE A WAGGY plus TE, the ends of tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the game away is to reveal a secret or plan by accident, as a loose-tongued person does.

clue.text: Over Ireland, aviator losing velocity switched from one plane to another

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the shuffled letters sit on top of the abbreviation for Ireland
losing means the letter for velocity is lost from the aviator's letters
switched means changed round, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A pilot flying over Ireland loses speed and transfers between aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: AVIATOR without V leaves AIATOR, which 'switched' rearranges to AIRTOA, placed over IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-to-air describes something, such as a missile or refuelling, passing between aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Disrupted the Riding Club?

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
a set is a social group or club, as in the jet set

explanation.surface: Asks whether the members of an equestrian club were thrown into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of mounted riders would be an 'up set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as a past participle means disturbed or thrown into disorder.

clue.text: What the Pied Piper did started a dispute

definitions.meaning: the Pied Piper of Hamelin led away all the town's children, its offspring
to begin arguing or object to something

explanation.surface: Recalls the folk tale of the piper who lured away Hamelin's children after a quarrel over payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue also means children or offspring, so the Piper literally took the town's issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Took issue means disagreed or argued; in the other sense issue means descendants.

clue.text: A bit of music making the house shake

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
to quaver is to shake or tremble

explanation.surface: Music played so loudly it makes the whole house tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is the British word for a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a short musical note, a sixteenth note, so a tiny bit of music.

clue.text: Extremely slothful old b——

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of slothful

parts.note: the dash stands for a censored rude word beginning with b, leaving only the letter itself

explanation.surface: Someone muttering a censored insult at a very lazy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also giving SL, O and the censored B.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person, exactly the sort described as slothful.

clue.text: My offer to pay brings forth abuse

definitions.meaning: said when offering to pick up the bill
to abuse is to treat badly

explanation.surface: An offer to pick up the bill unexpectedly leads to a torrent of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'LL TREAT, it is what you say when offering to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-treat means to treat cruelly, a synonym of the verb abuse.

clue.text: Get a bit lost in New Orleans on the way back

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the scrambled letters sit within the turned abbreviation
on the way back means going in reverse, so the abbreviation for New Orleans is read backwards
lost in the sense of astray or confused, signalling the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Advice to get a little lost in New Orleans while travelling home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' sounds like the travel advice but is the signal to scramble A BIT; the reversed abbreviation gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtain and get are synonyms meaning to acquire.

clue.text: Nerd offered wee bairns clothes

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means covers or dresses, so these words wrap the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A geek in Scotland donates clothing to small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is a verb: the words clothe the answer. BAIRNS is Scots for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a dull, socially awkward person, a slang synonym for nerd.

clue.text: Shooter leaves part of ship full of punctures extensively

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the second piece goes inside
leaves means departs from, so the word for shooter is removed

parts.note: the gunwale is the upper edge of a ship's side
a gun is a shooter
punctures are holes

explanation.surface: A ship's timbers riddled by gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: GUN 'leaves' GUNWALE to give WALE, which is 'full of' HOLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale used as an adverb means on a large scale, extensively and indiscriminately.

clue.text: Cup Final for one is team's day to be excited

indicators.note: to be excited means stirred up, signalling the letters are mixed

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter: the word team plus S

indicators.note: the final for a word is its last letter, here the end of one

explanation.surface: A cup final, for example, is the day a team gets thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup Final' reads as one phrase, but Cup is the definition. IS, TEAMS and D are shuffled into DEMITASS, and E, the end of one, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup, from French for half-cup.

clue.text: Prince supports amateur, potentially star material

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means sitting underneath, so the title comes below
potentially means what could be made from it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: khan is a title of a ruler or prince in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A royal backs a novice who could become a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' turns STAR into STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a fabric made from the curly fleece of young lambs, so a type of material.

clue.text: Mount Ida covered by corn and barley? That's infrequent

indicators.note: to mount is to climb, so in a down clue the assembled letters read upwards
covered by means enclosed within, so the name sits inside the produce

parts.note: corn and barley are examples of crops, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A Cretan mountain blanketed in fields of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount Ida' reads as the mountain, but 'Mount' says the whole assembly is read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals, which is the same as infrequent.

clue.text: High jinks in Equus?

definitions.meaning: Equus is Peter Shaffer's play about a boy and horses, so a play about horses

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there is mischief in a famous stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus, Latin for horse, is the title of a well-known play, so it is a horse play.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseplay is rough, boisterous fun, a synonym of high jinks.

clue.text: Abandon bow of boat, say

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter is abandoned

parts.note: a cutter is a small boat

explanation.surface: An order to abandon the front of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link word inviting an example, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or speak aloud.

clue.text: Accepting rising price, paid for explosive device

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the abbreviation holds the turned word

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the word for price is reversed

parts.note: a rate is a price, as in the going rate

explanation.surface: Someone takes a higher price and pays for a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RATE into ETAR, which PD is 'Accepting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard is a small bomb for blasting through doors, as in hoist with his own petard.

clue.text: Sound detector that may be used in church

definitions.text: that may be used in church

indicators.note: sound at the start signals that the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a sensor is a detector

explanation.surface: An acoustic sensor installed in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound detector' reads as a microphone, but 'Sound' is the signal and 'detector' is SENSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a vessel for burning incense, swung during religious services.

clue.text: Crouch End in riot after band finally cancelled

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the end of riot follows
the final letter is cancelled, removed

parts.note: a squad is a band or group of people

indicators.note: the end in a word is its last letter, here of riot

explanation.surface: Trouble in Crouch End, a north London district, after a group's concert is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crouch End' reads as the London place, but Crouch is the definition and End starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To squat is to crouch with the knees bent and heels close to the bottom.

clue.text: Klingsor is into rock, primarily Slade, Rolling Stones

indicators.note: rolling means tumbling about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter Klingsor refers to themself, so the word for the setter is me

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of rock

explanation.surface: The setter confesses a love of rock music, chiefly Slade and the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' reads as the band, but 'Rolling' shuffles ME, R and SLADE. Slade was a British glam-rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeralds are green precious stones.

clue.text: Contrarily, terminal for neutral (blue) is live

indicators.note: contrarily means the opposite way round, so the word for blue is read backwards

parts.note: blue means risqué or lewd

indicators.note: the terminal for a word is its final letter, here of neutral

explanation.surface: Electrical wiring: the blue wire is neutral, yet contrary to that it is live.
explanation.walkthrough: UK plug wiring makes blue the neutral and brown the live wire. 'Contrarily' turns LEWD into DWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, reside.

clue.text: Hawaiian island's coral oddly lost colour to a large extent

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are lost, leaving the second and fourth of coral
only a large part of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: hue is a colour or shade

explanation.surface: An island's coral has largely lost its colour, as in reef bleaching.
explanation.walkthrough: CORAL keeps its even letters O and A; HUE loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island where Honolulu stands.

clue.text: Description of mule worn out after covering much distance?

definitions.text: Description of mule worn out after covering much distance?

parts.words: Description of mule worn out after covering much distance?
parts.note: a mule, as a backless slipper or as a hard-walked animal, would be worn at the back of the foot after a long trek; the phrase also means shabby

explanation.surface: How a mule looks after a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule is both a pack animal and a backless slipper; either, after a long walk, would be worn at the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel means shabby or run-down, literally shoes worn down at the back.

clue.text: Derby County's foul overlooked at first

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east; the possessive adds no letter

indicators.note: the first letter is overlooked, left out

parts.note: yucky means foul or disgusting

explanation.surface: A football report on a Derby County player's foul that the referee missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby County' reads as the football club, but Derby is the definition. KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentucky Derby is the famous American horse race, so the state's name precedes Derby.

clue.text: Daughter connected to internet (not at home) having installed good computer accessory

indicators.note: having installed means containing, so the abbreviation for good goes inside
in means at home, so the letters IN are removed

parts.note: online means connected to the internet

explanation.surface: A daughter, online while out, has installed a decent gadget on the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: ONLINE without IN, the crossword sense of 'at home', leaves ONLE, which takes in G.
explanation.definitionFit: A dongle is a small device plugged into a computer port, such as a wireless adapter.
